## Chef's Note

Slice the flank steak across its visible muscle fibers, then distribute all the measured cornstarch over the slices. This is a shorter-cooking flank-steak recipe, distinct from the chuck-roast Korean beef. Keep the green onions for the finish and judge tenderness as well as temperature.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Use fully thawed flank steak kept refrigerated until preparation. Slice thinly against the grain. Check the cooker’s load instructions before starting; the listed batch is not proof that a particular large cooker is adequately filled.

2. **Coat:** Toss all the measured steak and cornstarch in a bowl until the slices are evenly coated. Transfer the coated steak and any remaining measured coating to the cooker.

3. **Add sauce:** Add all the sesame oil, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar and measured water. Stir to coat the meat, cover and start promptly.

4. **Cook:** Cover and cook on HIGH for 2–3 hours or LOW for 4–5 hours as planning ranges. Start with fully thawed beef. Check tenderness and that beef has reached at least 145°F / 63°C with three minutes rest before serving. The sauce should be thickened and the thin slices tender; continue as needed rather than rely only on the clock.

5. **Finish:** Stir in all the measured green onions, then divide among the listed portions and serve.

## Cooking Notes

Check the actual cooker’s instructions for its permitted food load, liquid requirements and meat size. A common Crock-Pot manual specifies half to three-quarters full, check your model’s own limits. When scaling, choose suitable cooker capacity or separate appropriately filled cookers, and divide all measured ingredients across them. Cooking times do not multiply with portions. Keep the lid closed except for necessary additions and doneness checks; cook on LOW or HIGH, not WARM.

Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Use within 3–4 days. Reheat on the stove, in the microwave or oven to 165°F / 74°C; do not use the slow cooker to reheat cold leftovers. If holding cooked food in the cooker, maintain at least 140°F / 60°C and follow its holding instructions.

sourceApplicability.title: Sara Welch — Slow cooker Mongolian beef
sourceApplicability.supports: Corroborates thin against-grain flank, full coating/sauce ingredients and both saved heat routes.
sourceApplicability.limits: No chuck substitution, extra slurry, forced sear or measured yield is inferred.

sourceApplicability.title: USDA — Slow cookers and food safety
sourceApplicability.supports: Fully thawed refrigerated meat/poultry, prompt cooking, actual appliance meat-size instructions, lid control, permissible LOW cooking, outside-cooker reheating to 165°F before holding at 140°F.
sourceApplicability.limits: Does not certify recipe ratios, universal fill percentages, household cooker identity, elapsed times, final yield or raw bean substitutions.

sourceApplicability.title: Crock-Pot — SCVCS603S operating manual example
sourceApplicability.supports: This particular model gives a half-to-three-quarter fill band and operating/holding instructions; its permitted minimum and maximum are model-specific examples.
sourceApplicability.limits: The household model is unknown. Follow its actual minimum/maximum, meat-size and liquid instructions; do not import the older frozen-meat suggestion or an arbitrary extra rice-liquid amount.

sourceApplicability.title: FoodSafety.gov — Safe minimum internal temperatures
sourceApplicability.supports: Chicken 165°F; beef/pork 145°F with three-minute rest; leftovers of any type 165°F.
sourceApplicability.limits: Tender chuck/shoulder may need substantially more cooking. No fixed slow-cooker clock, uniform tenderness or zero-risk guarantee follows.

sourceApplicability.title: USDA — Leftovers and food safety
sourceApplicability.supports: Prompt shallow cooling/refrigeration, 40°F refrigerator, 2-hour limit or 1 hour above 90°F, 3–4-day handling range, measured 165°F throughout; separately recommends a rolling boil for reheated soups, sauces and gravies.
sourceApplicability.limits: 165°F is a supported endpoint, not declared inaccurate. Additional liquid-specific guidance does not prescribe first-cook boiling, prolonged reduction, dilution, fat reduction, a new duration or unchanged dairy/starch texture. Direct FSIS fetch returned 403 during the prior review; official indexed passage was recovered.

sourceApplicability.title: FDA — Food Code 2022, §§3-403.10–.11
sourceApplicability.supports: Distinguishes food-service immediate service from reheating for hot holding, with separate time/temperature and microwave provisions.
sourceApplicability.limits: Comparison evidence only. Its food-service scope is not prescribed to household cooks; no 15-second public household rule was added.
